transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-13
Start: 16:10 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording id: ff-20250813-blueharbor-5392
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (BlueHarbor ML), Sara Patel (PM), Jonas Klein (Infra), Priya Shah (Security), Speaker 6

Summary:
- Goal: Understand integration options for BlueHarbor's patient-facing summarization and search features. Evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for security/compliance and integration patterns (SDKs vs gateway/proxy).
- Key constraints: PHI-like data, VPC peering preferred, 99th p95 latency targets ~250ms token generation for short chats, cost sensitivity at scale, strong audit/compliance needs (SOC2, encrypted logs, KMS).
- Decided next: POC with dedicated pools + gateway proxy pattern; SE to deliver LangChain connector example and gateway repo.

Topics covered:
1) High-level product fit (hosted/dedicated/private)
2) Integration patterns: direct SDK in app, gateway/proxy sidecar, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors
3) Network/security: VPC peering, outbound IPs, KMS, SAML/SSO, audit logs retention
4) Quotas/rate-limiting and multi-tenant routing
5) Observability hooks: tracing, token-level costs, error dashboards
6) Next steps and POC scope

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference and with me is Liam O'Connor, our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:00:10] Alex (BlueHarbor ML): Good, thanks. Running a little late but ready to jump in.
[00:00:15] Sara (PM): Hi all, Sara here. Wanted to make sure we cover integration patterns and the security checklist up front.
[00:00:22] Maya: Totally — we'll hit that. Quick round robin on what you folks are evaluating right now?
[00:00:29] Jonas (Infra): We're running a mix of on-prem and cloud. Primary ask is we can't send raw PHI outside our VPC without encryption and audit controls. We're looking at whether a hosted API with dedicated pools is enough, or we need a private deployment.
[00:00:41] Priya (Security): Also SAML SSO for console access, KMS integration for keys, and retention controls on logs.
[00:00:48] Liam (Redwood SE): Makes sense. At a high level, Redwood offers three lanes — Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + VPC peering), and Private (customer-managed control plane). For PHI workloads most folks start with Dedicated + VPC peering to avoid raw traffic over the public internet, unless they need air-gapped.
[00:01:10] Alex: If we did Dedicated, can we still use the standard SDKs? We use LangChain and a few custom agents with LlamaIndex.
[00:01:18] Liam: Yes — SDKs are identical across hosted and dedicated; the endpoint changes and you can pin model versions. LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors usually just point to the Redwood URL. We also provide an example connector repo and a gateway pattern if you want to centralize auth, rate limiting, and observability.
[00:01:34] Sara: Can you explain the gateway pattern? We currently have a microservice that brokers requests to multiple LLM providers.
[00:01:40] Liam: Sure. There are two main patterns we see: direct SDK integration — each service calls Redwood directly using the SDK or HTTP API — and gateway/proxy approach — a single internal gateway accepts calls from your services and shuttles them to Redwood. Gateway is useful for multi-tenant routing, centralized caching, prefix caching, and applying consistent rate limits or prompt transformations.
[00:01:58] Jonas: So the gateway would sit inside our VPC and outbound to Redwood's dedicated pool?
[00:02:03] Liam: Exactly. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering or private link, so traffic never traverses the public internet. The gateway talks to Redwood endpoints over that peered connection. It also simplifies auditing because you can log semantically at your boundary.
[00:02:17] Alex: One concern — how does KV cache and prefix caching behave with a gateway? We do long docs + chat flows.
[00:02:23] Liam: Good question. The runtime expects the KV cache to be managed per session/token. If your gateway aggregates sessions you need to ensure you forward the appropriate cache keys or keep sticky routing to the same worker to preserve performance. We provide examples of sticky session headers and cache APIs in the gateway repo. There's a tradeoff: centralized gateway can reduce request fanout and enable response-level caching, but it adds complexity to cache co-location.
[00:02:45] Sara: Are there existing LangChain adapters?
[00:02:48] Liam: Yes, we have a maintained LangChain connector and a LlamaIndex plugin example. I'll share a short demo repo that shows both patterns: direct SDK call from an app and a gateway shim that exposes a local restful API.
[00:02:59] Maya: Quick note — some of our customers run a small sidecar gateway per host (sidecar) instead of a centralized gateway. That reduces cross-host sticky routing complexity. It's more ops overhead but often more robust for KV cache locality.
[00:03:14] Alex: Helpful. On rate limits: we need per-customer quotas and burst handling, can Redwood support that at the gateway level or does it need to be in BlueHarbor infra?
[00:03:23] Liam: You can do both. Redwood has per-token and per-route quotas at the API level — you can configure rate limits per API key and setup fallback policies (e.g., degrade to smaller model). For fine-grained customer quotas we'd typically implement those in your gateway which then maps tenant->api-key. Redwood's console will still show token breakdown per api-key, so it's compatible.
[00:03:42] Priya: About audit logs — we need an immutable trail of which prompts were submitted and who accessed outputs for 7 years. Is that possible without storing raw prompts in your logs?
[00:03:51] Maya: We have options: you can emit hashed prompt fingerprints to Redwood logs and keep full prompts only in your sidecar gateway behind your KMS. With Dedicated/Private, you get more control and can route logs to your SIEM. We'll include the details in the SOC2 pack.
[00:04:05] Priya: Good. Any limitations on streaming or function-calling with Dedicated?
[00:04:10] Liam: No — streaming and function/tool-calls are supported across all deployment modes. Some kernel-level optimizations differ slightly depending on quantization and model variant but from the API surface it's feature-parity.
[00:04:21] Sara: Latency: we have an SLO of 250ms p95 for short chat replies (<64 tokens). Will dedicated pool meet that?
[00:04:29] Liam: We benchmark against that. It depends on model and batch sizing. For smaller models and optimized kernels, Dedicated with pinned workers can hit 99ms-150ms p95 for short sequences. We'll want to run a short benchmark with your prompt set.
[00:04:41] Alex: OK let's talk POC scope. We want: (1) LangChain-based search + summarization flow (2) gateway proxy to centralize tenant quotas and logging (3) observe token costs.
[00:04:52] Maya: Sounds good. Proposed POC: Redwood provides a dedicated pool for 2 weeks, SE runs benchmark, delivers a LangChain connector and gateway example, BlueHarbor runs sample traffic and we collect metrics (latency, token cost, errors). Does that align?
[00:05:05] Jonas: Yes, but network-wise we'll need a small set of outbound IPs and an envelope to present to compliance. We'll also need an option to keep raw prompts inside our VPC.
[00:05:13] Liam: For outbound IPs we can provide a static egress list for the dedicated installation; for Private we can keep everything in your network. We'll include network diagram guidance.
[00:05:21] Speaker 6: Quick question on quotas — if we map every tenant to an API key, will token-level billing be split on your end?
[00:05:28] Maya: Yes, billing and token analytics are surfaced per API key and per model. So if you mint one API key per tenant it's possible to break down usage per tenant. For huge tenant counts we recommend a hybrid approach: per-tenant internal throttles and batched reporting.
[00:05:42] Sara: Observability — what hooks do you provide? We use Datadog and have a tracing standard.
[00:05:47] Liam: We emit trace spans compatible with OpenTelemetry; you can attach your trace ids in requests and Redwood will attach server spans to the trace. We also expose per-route token cost breakdowns in the console and an API for exporting cost/time series.
[00:06:02] Alex: Does the SDK automatically forward trace headers or do we have to add them in our gateway?
[00:06:05] Liam: The SDK forwards common tracing headers if present; the gateway pattern is useful to guarantee propagation.
[00:06:11] Priya: For SAML/SSO — can we SSO into the Redwood Console while using Dedicated?
[00:06:16] Maya: Yes, Dedicated includes SSO support (SAML or OIDC), RBAC roles, and audit logs. For Private deployments, console access can be brokered through your IdP.
[00:06:27] Jonas: Is there a managed upgrade window? We need predictable maintenance scheduling.
[00:06:32] Liam: For Dedicated we offer scheduled maintenance windows and SLA-backed uptime. We'll catalog upgrade impact in the runbook we share.
[00:06:40] Sara: Pricing — can you give a rough delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[00:06:44] Maya: Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Dedicated is a reserved capacity subscription with a base monthly fee and usage tiers. We'll send a comparison matrix with numbers and an example spend for your expected token volume.
[00:06:56] Alex: Back to integration: our current agents use LangChain retriever pipelines with LlamaIndex storing vector embeddings. Does Redwood have an embeddings pipeline or recommended workflow?
[00:07:07] Liam: Redwood provides embeddings endpoints as well. For scale we recommend a pipeline: generate embeddings (batch), store vectors in your index (we've seen folks use Milvus/FAISS/Weaviate), then use LangChain retriever to build context windows. For RDW (redwood) we provide examples for batching embeddings and cost-aware recommendations.
[00:07:23] Alex: Any limit on embedding batch size?
[00:07:25] Liam: There's a practical limit tied to request size; defaults are safe but you can push larger batches with streaming. We'll share the best practices doc.
[00:07:31] Speaker 6: On the gateway repo you mentioned, what's the license? Can we run it internally?
[00:07:35] Liam: It's MIT-licensed reference code intended for internal use. We also provide a hardened example with auth and rate-limits as part of the enterprise repo.
[00:07:44] Priya: We also need to know what is stored in Redwood logs. Specifically, is there a way to redact PHI before it hits your logs?
[00:07:52] Maya: Yes. We have request-side filtering options in the gateway example where you can run a redaction step or hash before forwarding. For Dedicated we can also route logs to your SIEM via a secure connector, and you can choose not to store payloads centrally.
[00:08:03] Alex: For LlamaIndex, any gotchas? We've had tokenization differences across runtimes.
[00:08:08] Liam: Tokenization differences are model dependent. We recommend normalizing on the same tokenizer when possible and adding small validation tests in your CI for embeddings/vector drift. We can provide a compatibility checklist.
[00:08:19] Sara: OK practical sequence: we onboard, run a 2-week dedicated trial, integrate gateway, run benchmarks — who are the owners?
[00:08:27] Maya: Redwood: Maya (sales) handles contracting, Liam will lead the technical POC. BlueHarbor: Alex will own ML workload tests, Jonas infra will handle VPC peering, Priya will handle compliance signoff.
[00:08:37] Liam: I'll create a small checklist and sample GH repo: - langchain-connector example - gateway sidecar example - sticky session header patterns - telemetry hooks README
[00:08:48] Alex: Perfect. One more on fallback: If dedicated pool capacity is saturated, can we automatically fail over to a cheaper region or model?
[00:08:56] Liam: Yes; Redwood supports routing policies. You can configure fallbacks by model family or region and opt into automatic cost-based fallbacks. We log those events so you can analyze quality regressions.
[00:09:09] Jonas: Any additional network ports besides standard https egress?
[00:09:13] Liam: No, standard TLS over 443. For VPC peering there are some internal ports for health checks — we'll share precise runbook.
[00:09:22] Sara: Let's reprioritize: POC success metrics?
[00:09:25] Alex: Latency p95 <= 250ms for short chats, embedding throughput >= 500 docs/min, cost <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll send exact), and verification of logs/retention flows.
[00:09:38] Maya: Great — we'll bake those into the POC charter.
[00:09:40] Speaker 6: Any examples of customers using sidecar + LangChain at scale?
[00:09:44] Liam: Yes — one fintech customer uses sidecars per host to keep KV caches local and uses a central billing export to their ledger. They chose dedicated pools for predictable tail latencies.
[00:09:57] Priya: We might also want an air-gapped option for one business line — what does Private look like?
[00:10:02] Maya: Private is essentially the same control plane but deployed in your environment or managed in a VPC where you control egress. It includes enterprise support and full network isolation. We can discuss an on-prem package if needed.
[00:10:14] Alex: Any timeline to stand up a dedicated test pool?
[00:10:17] Maya: Typical lead time is 2–3 weeks after contract for dedicated. For Private it's longer. For the POC we can provision a temporary dedicated pool faster if paperwork is signed.
[00:10:28] Sara: Let's capture the open questions: (1) network egress list (2) storage of prompts/logs plan (3) exact pricing delta — we'll need numbers to present to legal and procurement.
[00:10:37] Maya: Noted — I'll send the price matrix and security pack by Friday.
[00:10:41] Liam: I'll push the GH repos and sample benchmark script.
[00:10:46] Alex: We'll gather prompt samples and the token distribution.
[00:10:50] Jonas: I'll prepare the infra diagram and compliance checklist.
[00:10:54] Maya: Anything else before we close?
[00:10:56] Priya: One minor — do you have an SLA for redact requests / log deletion?
[00:11:01] Maya: Yes, for Dedicated we can commit deletion windows and provide a runbook. We'll include specifics.
[00:11:07] Speaker 6: Cool.
[00:11:10] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule a POC kickoff.
[00:11:15] Alex: Thanks all.

[00:11:16] -- End of main discussion; remaining ~43 min were Q&A and deeper tech notes (partial transcript below) --
[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Liam (Redwood SE): (digs into gateway code) so in the example you see header X-RW-SESSION to sticky the session to the worker, and we use OTEL trace-id to connect traces.
[00:12:12] [00:12:12] Alex: yeah okay so X-RW-SESSION is our token id, if we forward that we maintain KV locality.
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Liam: Right. And here's a small snippet for exponential backoff with queueing so you don't blow up queues when bursty traffic hits. The gateway can do model multiplexing — for embeddings we batch, for generation we route to low-latency workers.
[00:13:05] [00:13:05] Jonas: If we do sidecars, how do we distribute models? Do sidecars hot-swap model versions?
[00:13:11] Liam: Sidecars can pin model versions and we can push deprecations; the runtime supports graceful model swaps. We'll log a model version header so you can reconcile outputs.
[00:13:28] [00:13:28] Alex: A lot of our prompts include patient context. We're cautious about sending entire docs. Would you recommend redaction in the gateway before forwarding?
[00:13:36] Liam: Yes — redact or hash sensitive identifiers in the gateway; then forward hashed values for correlation. For evaluation we can run an internal lab that uses synthetic PII to measure effect on quality.
[00:14:02] [00:14:02] Maya: We have a small bench spreadsheet that maps token cost to model and quantization; I'll attach it.
[00:14:12] [00:14:12] Alex: Do you support quantized model variants in Dedicated?
[00:14:16] Liam: Yes, quantized variants are supported; the runtime picks kernels accordingly. We'll recommend quantization based on your quality budget.
[00:14:28] [00:14:28] Priya: For KMS — can keys be customer-managed?
[00:14:31] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private can integrate with your KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest and key lifecycle management.
[00:14:38] [00:14:38] Sara: What about cost visibility at the route level?
[00:14:41] Liam: Console shows token cost per route and per key; you can also pull raw usage via API. We'll show you the console during the POC.
[00:15:05] [00:15:05] Alex: Any gotchas with LangChain Chains that call tools? We do tool-calling extensively.
[00:15:12] Liam: Tools and function-calling are first-class; gateway needs to carefully forward tool-calls and manage auth for external tools. For example, if your chain calls a retrieval service we recommend keeping those calls internal to BlueHarbor and only send the assembled context to Redwood.
[00:15:31] [00:15:31] Jonas: If we want to audit who requested what per patient, do you surface user-id with the log events?
[00:15:38] Liam: We can include metadata headers like X-User-Id in logs or send them hashed; we'll coordinate the format with you.
[00:15:50] [00:15:50] Priya: A note — our legal team will ask for indemnities around PHI; is Redwood comfortable with that?
[00:15:55] Maya: We have enterprise terms and can work with your legal on standard clauses. We'll surface precedent contracts.
[00:16:05] [00:16:05] Alex: Any internal rate-limiting options in SDK? e.g., token bucket client-side?
[00:16:10] Liam: SDK has an optional client-side rate limiter and retry middleware. For large fleets we prefer edge/gateway throttles.
[00:16:21] [00:16:21] Speaker 6: For observability, can we get raw token streams back to our tracing?
[00:16:26] Liam: We can stream token deltas to your OTEL collector; for PHI you may want to only stream token counts not raw tokens.
[00:16:36] [00:16:36] Maya: We're going to compile all of this into a POC charter and runbook.
[00:16:40] [00:16:40] Alex: Thanks, we'll review.
